quarterly_data.signal: Trial designs: President of R&D Don Bergstrom said the Phase III ReDiscover-2 trial enrolls patients previously treated with endocrine therapy and a CDK4/6 inhibitor, excluding patients with multiple prior CDK4/6 inhibitors or an ADC, and is powered to show clinically meaningful improvement in PFS with OS as a key secondary endpoint. Chief Corporate Development Officer Peter Rahmer said zovegalisib entered the clinic in vascular anomalies in the spring of 2025; the ReInspire dose-randomized portion tested 100 milligrams BID, 300 milligrams BID and 400 milligrams BID in patients 12 years and older, 20 of the 32 patients were efficacy evaluable at the ISSVA disclosure in May (about four months of median follow-up), and all 32 will be efficacy evaluable by the year-end disclosure, alongside early expansion data; a responder is a target lesion shrinking by 20% or greater. For full approval Relay would propose continuing single-arm enrollment inside ReInspire, subject to FDA discussion. On pricing precedent he cited alpelisib at $25,000 a month as Piqray in breast cancer and $36,000 a month as Vijoice in vascular anomalies, while calling zovegalisib pricing premature.
quarterly_data.figure: 20 of 32 patients efficacy evaluable at ISSVA; about four months median follow-up; response = lesion shrinkage of 20% or greater; Piqray $25,000 a month vs Vijoice $36,000 a month
